maria_gonzalez: FYI customer reported partial chat output over both SSE and websocket after the 03/15 deploy. They see last 1-3 tokens missing and then connection closes. Request IDs I have so far: req_01F2A3X, req_01F2A3Y. Logs show regular chunk flushes but the final chunk seems empty. Can someone take a look?

kevin_liu: Can you paste the exact curl you used to repro and the client env? any proxies or CDNs in front (CF, Fastly)?

maria_gonzalez: curl I used (minimal):

```
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/chat/stream -d '{"model":"rwd-small","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"tell me a short story"}]}'
```

Client is behind Cloudflare + an internal nginx reverse proxy (we sit in front of workers). Customer tested with curl -N and still saw truncated ending.

alex_chang: nginx will buffer and coalesce by default. Try adding `X-Accel-Buffering: no` on the response path or set `proxy_buffering off` for the location. Also ensure the response headers: `Content-Type: text/event-stream` + `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and `Cache-Control: no-transform` so intermediaries don't re-chunk. Can you paste the worker log segment for one of the request IDs?

maria_gonzalez: pasting worker log around req_01F2A3X:

```
[2026-03-16T14:22:10.123Z] req=req_01F2A3X worker=wrkr-07 EMIT_CHUNK size=512 time=14:22:10.125
[2026-03-16T14:22:10.623Z] req=req_01F2A3X worker=wrkr-07 EMIT_CHUNK size=480 time=14:22:10.625
[2026-03-16T14:22:11.130Z] req=req_01F2A3X worker=wrkr-07 EMIT_CHUNK size=96 time=14:22:11.131
[2026-03-16T14:22:11.131Z] req=req_01F2A3X worker=wrkr-07 FLUSH_SENT bytes=1188
[2026-03-16T14:22:11.132Z] req=req_01F2A3X worker=wrkr-07 CONNECTION_CLOSE code=200
```

looks like our runtime emitted chunks then closed. customer still missing last token.

ops_bot: deploy:canary 2026-03-15T21:02 succeeded on cluster-west (id: dep_20260315_2102) :white_check_mark:

kevin_liu: two things to validate: 1) whether worker really sent the final bytes (tcpdump/ngrep on worker side) and 2) whether any proxy/CDN trimmed trailing chunk on close. Repro steps I'd try locally:

```
# SSE repro using curl
curl -N -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOK' \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-small","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"short"}]}' \
  https://<api-host>/v1/chat/stream

# For websocket
websocat -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOK' ws://<host>/v1/chat/ws
```

Also try `curl --resolve api.host:443:<worker-ip>` to bypass CF.

maria_gonzalez: adding another id: req_01F2A3Z. Customer says when they pipe output to a file it's complete, but when their Node websocket client consumes the stream it drops last 1-2 tokens. They saw same behavior from a direct `curl --resolve` run too. I'm assembling a debug bundle (ngrep/tcpdump + nginx conf + worker logs) now.

alex_chang: when you gather bundle include: nginx location conf (check `proxy_buffering off; proxy_set_header Connection "keep-alive"; proxy_http_version 1.1;`), and the exact response headers from worker for that request id. If nginx is between CF and worker we should capture both sides. For tcpdump use `tcpdump -w sse-req.pcap host <client-ip> and port 443` and also `ngrep -W byline -d any port 443` if you can strip TLS (or use a test VM with TLS terminated).

kevin_liu: our SSE flusher code had a past issue where it would write a zero-length chunk prior to close in some timing windows, causing some clients to treat stream as truncated. I'll try to reproduce with a small python server that sends chunks then closes immediately to see how Node ws client behaves. If server sent final bytes, then it's either CF/nginx or the client.

maria_gonzalez: bundle uploaded to internal share: https://redwood-internal/sup-debug/1900501234-bundle.tar.gz (contains nginx.conf, worker_logs_tail, tcpdump.pcap, reproduce_curl.sh). Tagging kevin_liu and alex_chang.

alex_chang: :thumbsup: I'll spin up a nginx test VM and try to reproduce with our proxy settings. If we can reproduce with nginx alone we can propose `proxy_buffering off` as mitigation.

kevin_liu: if you want a quick local check, run this python SSE app to simulate flush behavior:

```
python - <<'PY'
import time,sys
print('Content-Type: text/event-stream\n')
for i in range(3):
    sys.stdout.write(f"data: token-{i} \n\n")
    sys.stdout.flush()
    time.sleep(0.5)
# close without extra newline
sys.exit(0)
PY
```

Then `curl -N` vs a Node stream consumer and compare. If Node drops last token but curl-to-file keeps it, likely client parsing/buffering.

maria_gonzalez: customer will try the python test and also send us their Node client code sample. For now we have logs + bundle + reproduce steps. Thanks all — will update thread when customer runs tests.
